overview: South32 is a diversified mining and metals company, demerged from BHP in 2015, that mines and processes bauxite, alumina, aluminium, copper, manganese, zinc, lead and silver across the Americas, Australia and Southern Africa. It reports in US dollars with a June fiscal year end and is listed on the ASX, LSE and JSE (ADR: SOUHY). On 30 June 2026 South32 agreed to sell its entire aluminium value chain (Worsley Alumina, Hillside Aluminium, MRN bauxite, Brazil Alumina and Brazil Aluminium) to Alcoa Corporation for up to US$5.6 billion, a transaction expected to complete in H2 FY27 that will re-position the company as an upstream base-metals producer (copper, zinc, silver, lead) alongside a large manganese business.

business_model.summary: South32 makes money by mining and processing bulk and base metal commodities and selling them into global markets at prevailing (largely USD-denominated) commodity prices; there is no recurring/subscription revenue -- it is a price-taker, volume-and-cost-driven commodity producer with earnings highly leveraged to spot prices for aluminium, alumina, copper, zinc, manganese and silver. Following the FY26 Alcoa agreement and the FY25 divestments of Illawarra Metallurgical Coal (Aug 2024) and Cerro Matoso nickel (Dec 2025), the portfolio is being actively reshaped toward higher-margin base and precious metals.

business_model.customer_type: B2B - global industrial/commodity customers (smelters, steel mills, battery/cathode makers, trading houses); commodities sold on global exchange-linked or contract pricing
business_model.geographic_mix: Operations in Australia, Southern Africa (South Africa, Mozambique), South America (Chile, Colombia, Brazil, Argentina), and North America (Arizona/Hermosa, Alaska/Ambler); Illawarra coal (Australia) and Cerro Matoso (Colombia) divested FY25/FY26; post-Alcoa-completion the aluminium value chain assets in Australia, Brazil and Mozal (South Africa/Mozambique JV, excluded from sale) exit the portfolio

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier diversified miner; globally significant producer of manganese ore (Australia Manganese and South Africa Manganese together make it one of the largest seaborne manganese suppliers) and a meaningful producer of alumina/aluminium (pending divestment) and silver/lead/zinc (Cannington is one of the world's highest-grade silver-lead-zinc mines); minority (45%) stakeholder in the large Sierra Gorda copper mine in Chile, not an operator

moat_factors.description: Cannington is a high-grade, high-margin zinc-lead-silver mine (53% operating margin in H1 FY26); Sierra Gorda delivered a 68% EBITDA margin in H1 FY26, reflecting favorable cost position, though these are asset-specific rather than company-wide advantages
Combined Australian and South African manganese operations give South32 meaningful influence over a concentrated global seaborne manganese market, a key steel and battery input

moat_factors.factor: Long-life reserve base and growth optionality
moat_factors.description: Hermosa's Taylor deposit (extended to ~33-year mine life), Ambler Metals (Alaska), and Sierra Gorda's fourth grinding line provide multi-decade production and optionality, though most require large, multi-year capital commitments before generating cash
Net debt of only US$25M at Dec-2025, an active US$2.6B capital-return program, and the Alcoa deal (which also removes ~US$1.1-1.2B of rehabilitation liabilities) support financial flexibility

weaknesses: No pricing power - a pure price-taker on globally-traded commodities with cost, not brand, as the main lever
Minority, non-operated stakes in several key assets (Sierra Gorda 45%, Ambler Metals 50%, Brazil Alumina/Aluminium JVs), limiting operational control

Post-Alcoa-completion the portfolio becomes materially smaller and more concentrated (~85% of earnings from base/precious metals), increasing single-commodity and single-asset (Sierra Gorda, Cannington, Hermosa) concentration risk

History of operational disruptions - Tropical Cyclone Megan at Australia Manganese, Mozal Aluminium power curtailment/care & maintenance, and a fatality at Worsley Alumina (Mar-2026) highlight execution and safety risk

Hermosa Taylor project capex has already grown by ~US$1.1B versus original approval (to ~US$3.3B) with first production pushed out from FY28 to H1 FY29 (full capacity FY31), evidencing execution/cost-overrun risk on its flagship growth project

growth_drivers: Alcoa transaction (announced 30 Jun 2026, ~US$5.6B, completion H2 FY27) reshapes South32 into a higher-margin, base-metals-focused producer, expected to lift base/precious metals' share of earnings to ~85% pro-forma and free up balance sheet capacity for growth and returns

Hermosa Taylor zinc-lead-silver project construction (federal NEPA permitting completed Jul-2026; Notice to Proceed expected Q1 FY27) - expected to almost double Group silver production once ramped, with adjacent Peake copper and Clark manganese deposits offering further optionality

Sierra Gorda fourth grinding line - feasibility study advancing, targeting ~20% increase in plant throughput and ~30% increase in copper-equivalent production from FY31, subject to a joint venture partner FID expected mid-CY26
Cannington underground Ore Reserve increased 28% in H1 FY26, extending mine life ~2 years to FY33, with additional underground and open-pit growth options under study

Ambler Metals (Alaska) - US Government support for the Ambler Access Road (Oct-2025) and Arctic deposit's acceptance into the FAST-41 covered-projects program (May-2026) are unlocking a high-grade copper/zinc growth option; approved/under-construction projects across the portfolio are expected to grow copper-equivalent production by ~55%
Secular demand tailwinds - copper, zinc, silver and manganese are all positioned as critical inputs to electrification, EVs, renewable energy, AI/data-centre buildout and battery technology
Capital management - ordinary dividend policy of minimum 40% of Underlying earnings, plus an active buyback/capital-return program (extended to Sept-2027, US$209M remaining as of FY26 year-end)

business.description: Earnings are directly exposed to volatile global prices for alumina, aluminium, copper, zinc, manganese and silver; H1 FY26 alumina price fell 27% YoY, cutting alumina EBITDA by US$365M even as base metals prices rose

business.risk: Hermosa/Taylor execution and cost overrun risk
business.description: Taylor's growth capex has risen by ~US$1.1B to ~US$3.3B and first production has slipped from the original schedule to H1 FY29 (full capacity FY31), driven by contractor productivity issues, inflation and tariff-driven input cost increases
Large stakes in Sierra Gorda (45%) and Ambler Metals (50%) mean South32 does not control operating decisions, capital allocation timing or cost outcomes at some of its most important growth assets

The sale requires South32 shareholder approval and other conditions precedent; expected to complete in H2 FY27, leaving execution, timing, and final consideration (up to US$5.6B, contingent elements) at risk of delay or adjustment
Recent disruptions include Tropical Cyclone Megan's impact on Australia Manganese, Mozal Aluminium's move to care and maintenance (power supply), and a fatality at Worsley Alumina in March 2026

financial.description: Revenue and costs are exposed to AUD, ZAR, BRL and CLP movements against the USD reporting currency; a stronger South African rand and Brazilian real reduced H1 FY26 EBIT by US$25M

General inflation across Australia, South America and Southern Africa, plus tariff-driven increases in steel, concrete and electrical components, reduced FY26 earnings and inflated Hermosa's growth capex

Underlying effective tax rate of 34.2% in H1 FY26 reflects multiple high-tax/royalty jurisdictions (Australia Manganese royalty-related tax of 20% of adjusted EBIT; Sierra Gorda royalty-related tax of 5-14%)

regulatory.description: Growth projects depend on permitting and government support across the US (Hermosa NEPA, Ambler Access Road, FAST-41), Chile, Australia and Southern Africa; the Alcoa transaction also requires various regulatory clearances across the jurisdictions in which the aluminium assets operate

Target to halve Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY35 (from FY21 levels) and reach net zero by 2050 requires ongoing capital investment in decarbonisation; a non-binding Climate Change Action Plan resolution passed with 90% shareholder support in Oct-2025, but future capex/compliance costs remain a variable

Mine closure and rehabilitation obligations are significant (Alcoa is assuming ~US$1.1-1.2B of rehabilitation provisions as part of the aluminium sale), and other operations carry similar long-dated environmental liabilities

macro.description: Prices for alumina, aluminium, copper, zinc and manganese are highly sensitive to Chinese industrial demand and global growth expectations, as well as supply-side dynamics in those commodity markets

macro.risk: Energy costs and security of supply
macro.description: Mozal Aluminium was forced into care and maintenance in March 2026 due to an inability to secure sufficient, affordable electricity - illustrating energy security/cost risk for energy-intensive smelting operations generally

macro.risk: Interest rate and capital markets sensitivity
macro.description: Net debt is low (US$25M at Dec-2025) limiting direct rate sensitivity, though large growth capex programs (Hermosa, Sierra Gorda) are sensitive to the cost and availability of capital and to commodity price assumptions underpinning project returns

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Diversified mining sector outlook is mixed: bulk/alumina prices have retreated from elevated levels while base and precious metals (copper, zinc, silver) have strengthened on electrification, AI/data-centre and renewable energy demand narratives; South32 is deliberately rotating its portfolio toward the latter
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - commodity price cycles drive earnings volatility across all segments; South32's FY26 results show earnings swinging materially between segments (alumina down sharply, base metals and manganese up) within a single half-year
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct balance-sheet sensitivity given low net debt, but moderate indirect sensitivity via the cost of capital for large development projects (Hermosa) and via the impact of rates on global growth/commodity demand
key_input_costs: Electricity (critical for aluminium smelting - Hillside, Mozal)
Coke and other smelter raw materials
Steel, concrete and electrical components for construction (Hermosa)

recent_developments.event: US Government announced authorisations for the Ambler Access Road, a key enabler for the Ambler Metals copper/zinc joint venture in Alaska
Non-binding shareholder resolution on South32's second Climate Change Action Plan passed AGM with 90% support
Completed divestment of Cerro Matoso (Colombian ferronickel operation) to a subsidiary of CoreX Holding B.V., further streamlining the portfolio toward base metals
Announced Mozal Aluminium would transition to care and maintenance around 15 March 2026 due to inability to secure sufficient, affordable electricity; divestment now under active consideration

H1 FY26 results: Underlying EBITDA up 9% to US$1,107M, Underlying earnings up 16% to US$435M, interim dividend of 3.9 US cents/share (40% payout), net debt of only US$25M; Cannington underground Ore Reserve increased 28%, extending mine life to FY33; capital management program increased by US$100M to US$2.6B
Mozal Aluminium placed on care and maintenance; a fatality occurred at Worsley Alumina in Western Australia
Board leadership transition: Stephen Pearce became Chair (replacing Karen Wood AM); Matt Daley joined as Deputy CEO ahead of becoming CEO

Hermosa Taylor project update: operating life extended 5 years to ~33 years, Ore Reserve/Mineral estimates up 52% to 99Mt, but growth capex raised by ~US$1.1B to ~US$3.3B and first production pushed to H1 FY29 (full capacity FY31) due to contractor productivity challenges, inflation and tariffs; Peake copper deposit Mineral Resource up 32%
Ambler Metals' Arctic polymetallic deposit accepted as a covered project under the US FAST-41 program, accelerating federal permitting

Entered binding conditional agreement to sell the aluminium value chain (Worsley Alumina, Hillside Aluminium, MRN bauxite stake, Brazil Alumina and Brazil Aluminium JVs) to Alcoa Corporation for up to US$5.6 billion, plus Alcoa assuming ~US$1.1-1.2B of rehabilitation provisions; expected to complete H2 FY27 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval; Matt Daley assumed CEO role effective 1 July 2026, succeeding Graham Kerr
US Forest Service issued the Final Record of Decision for Hermosa, completing NEPA federal permitting; Notice to Proceed on track for Q1 FY27

FY26 full-year results: Underlying EBITDA up 28% to US$2,462M, Underlying earnings up 55% to US$1,032M, full-year dividend up 55% to 9.3 US cents/share, free cash flow up to US$610M; capital management program extended to Sept-2027 (US$209M remaining); shares reached a 10-year high (~A$5.09) with ~43% YTD gains amid the base-metals re-rating narrative

guidance.management_commentary: Incoming CEO Matt Daley (effective 1 July 2026) emphasized 'creating a simpler, stronger business and delivering our growth projects,' with priorities centred on completing the Alcoa sale, progressing Hermosa, and growing base metals exposure. Chair Stephen Pearce noted the Alcoa transaction 'is a step change... that accelerates the delivery of our strategy and provides additional balance sheet flexibility to invest in our next phase of growth, while delivering shareholder returns.' Management flagged that FY26 production guidance was largely unchanged across operated businesses at the H1 mark, and that Taylor's capex increase and schedule slip reflect industry-wide inflation, contractor productivity and US tariff impacts rather than asset quality issues.

bull_case: Transformational Alcoa transaction (up to US$5.6B, completing H2 FY27) sheds the lower-margin, capital-intensive aluminium value chain and ~US$1.1-1.2B of rehabilitation liabilities, leaving a simpler, higher-margin base-metals-and-manganese portfolio (~85% of pro-forma earnings from base/precious metals) that could re-rate toward peer base-metals multiples

Strong balance sheet (net debt just US$25M at Dec-2025) and an active, extended capital-return program (US$2.6B total, US$209M remaining through Sept-2027) support shareholder returns even while funding growth capex

Multiple base-metals growth options - Sierra Gorda's fourth grinding line (~30% copper-equivalent uplift from FY31), Cannington's extended mine life (to FY33) and open-pit optionality, and Hermosa's Taylor/Peake/Clark polymetallic deposits - position South32 to benefit from secular electrification, AI/data-centre and renewable-energy demand for copper, zinc, silver and manganese

FY26 delivered record profitability (Underlying EBITDA +28% to US$2,462M, Underlying earnings +55% to US$1,032M) and the share price reached a 10-year high (~43% YTD gain to Aug-2026), evidencing strong operating momentum and market recognition of the portfolio shift
Manganese scale (Australia + South Africa) gives South32 a strategically significant position in a commodity increasingly valued for battery cathode chemistries and steel demand
bear_case: Flagship Hermosa/Taylor growth project has already seen capex balloon by ~US$1.1B to ~US$3.3B and first production slip to H1 FY29 (full capacity FY31), raising doubts about management's ability to deliver large projects on time and budget, with further slippage a real risk given contractor productivity and tariff-driven cost pressure

Post-Alcoa-completion earnings concentration rises sharply (~85% from base/precious metals), meaning a downturn in copper, zinc or silver prices would hit a much larger share of Group earnings with less diversification cushion than before
Key growth assets (Sierra Gorda 45%, Ambler Metals 50%) are non-operated joint ventures, limiting South32's control over capital allocation, cost management and development timing

Consensus analyst price targets (~A$4.84-5.09) sit close to or slightly below the recent share price (~A$5.09-5.16), suggesting the market may have already priced in much of the transformation story, leaving limited near-term upside absent further commodity price strength or upside surprises

Operational and safety disruptions recur across the portfolio - Mozal Aluminium's care-and-maintenance due to power supply issues, Tropical Cyclone Megan's earlier impact on Australia Manganese, and a fatality at Worsley Alumina - underscoring execution and ESG/safety risk inherent to a geographically dispersed, multi-commodity mining operation
